pr_title: HTTP/3: Use HTTPS options from listener
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/30770

Remove TLS configuration from QUIC options, which are global to a server, and get TLS configuration from `UseHttps`.
pr_comments: What does configuration look like now for an HTTP/3 endpoint?
What happens if you don't call UseHttps? That does seem a bit non obvious that it's needed but it's not that QUIC will pick up default certificate settings.

> What happens if you don't call UseHttps? That does seem a bit non obvious that it's needed but it's not that QUIC will pick up default certificate settings.

A friendly error message if a HTTP/3 endpoint doesn't have `UseHttps` makes sense. Is that what you're getting at?

I talked with msquic to match our TLS options with theirs. I have an issue that has a full list - https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/30857

The msquic version .NET is using at the moment is out of date. Any work to improve TLS option integration will wait until after it is updated. I'd like to merge this initial PR now, and then improve TLS support in the future.

@JamesNK I agree that adding support for new properties can wait. At this point I'd suggest we let @halter73 at least see the PR when he's back Monday, and in the meantime address a few of the failure scenarios like UseHttps not being called. It also looks like Helix needs re-running.

Adding some folks who may have insight here... @scalablecory @wfurt @ManickaP @CarnaViire 

My understanding here is that we intend to support SslServerAuthenticationOptions to the extent possible. If there are things that are supported by SslServerAuthenticationOptions that we can't support via MSQuic, then we should either fix those in MSQuic (ideally), or document them clearly and throw exceptions that point users in the right direction.

> TLS feature break down issue - #30857

This is great. We should be tracking this in dotnet/runtime.

issue_context.title: HTTP/3: Per-endpoint TLS configuration
issue_context.body: Today the TLS cert is configured once on the QUIC transport. Need to support endpoint specific TLS certificate config using `UseHttps`.

review_comments:
Can ALPN be customized on a listener today?

I left this global for now because I assume it will be removed once HTTP/3 is finalized.

ALPN can be customized in one of the callbacks that lets you specify the SslServerAuthenticationOptions.
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/b86257101783524b0bad3287dbb50af869a3db56/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/HttpsConnectionAdapterOptions.cs#L93

Yeah, I believe so: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Net.Quic/src/System/Net/Quic/Implementations/MsQuic/MsQuicListener.cs#L169.

I believe we can set the ALPN here to the right value.

We currently pass that type down to msquic as well: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Net.Quic/src/System/Net/Quic/Implementations/MsQuic/MsQuicListener.cs#L31. Again probably just some work to expose it correctly.

Not all of the UseHttps overloads share this code path.
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/0eb496acb249164668e6d889c7e8d3fe4d38da1b/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/ListenOptionsHttpsExtensions.cs#L243

MSQuic doesn't support Per-SNI callbacks, right? How do we communicate that at config time?

I think we need to figure this out.

cc @geoffkizer

If per-SNI callbacks aren't supported then it is a simple matter to throw an error if `ServerCertificate` is null. Should raise with msquic that it is something we'd want in the future.

If they are supported then we'll need to get the details from msquic and plum support for it through the various layers.

> MSQuic doesn't support Per-SNI callbacks, right? How do we communicate that at config time?

Clarify what you mean here? Do you mean selecting a certificate based on SNI? I believe MsQuic does support this, we just don't currently support it in System.Net.Quic.
That's a start, but in 5.0 SslStream added the ability to specify all TLS settings per SNI, not just the certificate. That's the overload I linked above.

There are a number of callbacks in our TLS support. I'm not experience in this area so I'd like to come up a list of what they're each called, how important it is to support them, and whether msquic can support them today.

Here is our list of UseHttps methods:

https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.hosting.listenoptionshttpsextensions?view=aspnetcore-5.0

---

There is UseHttps overload with a ServerSelectionCallback - https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.hosting.listenoptionshttpsextensions.usehttps?view=aspnetcore-5.0#Microsoft_AspNetCore_Hosting_ListenOptionsHttpsExtensions_UseHttps_Microsoft_AspNetCore_Server_Kestrel_Core_ListenOptions_System_Net_Security_ServerOptionsSelectionCallback_System_Object_

`public delegate ValueTask<SslServerAuthenticationOptions> ServerOptionsSelectionCallback(SslStream stream, SslClientHelloInfo clientHelloInfo, object? state, CancellationToken cancellationToken);`

Does it make sense to allow configuring TLS for QUIC using this callback? There won't be an SslStream. Might be able to get `SslClientHelloInfo` from msquic. I'm not sure.

---

Then there is the `ServerCertificateSelector` callback on the Https options type. https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/servers/kestrel/endpoints?view=aspnetcore-5.0#configure-endpoints-using-server-name-indication

---

`SslServerAuthenticationOptions.RemoteCertificateValidationCallback`

https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.security.sslserverauthenticationoptions.remotecertificatevalidationcallback?view=net-5.0#System_Net_Security_SslServerAuthenticationOptions_RemoteCertificateValidationCallback
Does IsTls become HttpsOptions != null?
The UseHttps overloads that setup a `ServerSelectionCallback` don't set this field.
That seems like a bug in those overloads?

I mean `HttpsOptions`. It will still be null because its creation is delayed until the connection is created.

Still need IsTls for that situation. In the future I think the callback will also be capture in which case:
`public bool IsTls => HttpsOptions != null || HttpOptionsCallback != null;`
@jkotalik What did these cert file path options do? I saw they were passed all the way into msquic
These were used for limitations in msquic, not accepting a x509 cert handle at the time. We should remove this though; it was a temporary work around.
We should confirm that either this now does work with msquic, or have a feature ask for them.

There are a lot of HTTPS options available on HttpsConnectionAdapterOptions.

Which are valid for HTTP/3 and msquic?
Assume all of them are relevant until proven otherwise. If something isn't supported by MSQuic then we need a good explanation of why and it should be documented on those options.
Issue to support all relevent options: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/30857
